result.description: BEHL HOLDINGS PTY LTD  As a Family Support Worker at BEHL HOLDINGS PTY LTD, you will provide practical and emotional support to individuals and families, helping them achieve greater independence and wellbeing. You will assist clients in accessing community services, implementing support plans, promoting positive outcomes, and maintaining accurate records while working collaboratively with families, healthcare professionals, and community organisations to deliver person-centred care.      Benefits   Competitive salary package   Supportive and inclusive team environment   Ongoing training and professional development   Career growth opportunities   Flexible work arrangements where applicable   Employee wellbeing support   Meaningful and rewarding work   Diverse and collaborative workplace   Paid leave entitlements   Stable, long-term employment opportunities    Task & responsibilities   Conduct comprehensive assessments to identify the social, emotional, behavioural and practical support needs of individuals and families, and develop person-centred support plans tailored to their goals and circumstances.  Coordinate referrals to appropriate health, mental health, housing, disability, education, employment and other community services to ensure clients receive holistic and timely support.  Deliver ongoing family support, parenting guidance and practical assistance to promote independence, resilience, child wellbeing and positive family functioning.  Monitor, review and document clients' progress against established support plans, maintaining accurate case notes and preparing reports in accordance with organisational policies and funding requirements.  Assist young people experiencing social, emotional, educational or financial difficulties by providing mentoring, advocacy, crisis support and referrals to specialist services where required.  Prepare case reports, funding documentation, service reviews and other administrative records to meet legislative, contractual and organisational requirements.  Liaise with community organisations, welfare agencies, government departments, healthcare professionals and other stakeholders to facilitate integrated service delivery and advocate for clients' needs.  Assess community needs and available resources to connect clients with suitable programs, financial assistance, training opportunities and support services that enhance social inclusion and wellbeing.  Promote awareness of available community resources, support services and educational programs through client engagement and collaboration with local service providers.  Interview clients and their families to assess the nature and extent of challenges affecting their wellbeing, including housing, financial hardship, family relationships, disability, and community participation.  Ensure all services are delivered in accordance with child protection legislation, disability standards, workplace health and safety requirements, privacy obligations and organisational policies while maintaining a client-centred, culturally respectful and ethical approach.  Support children, young people, older persons and individuals with disability by providing practical assistance, life skills development, community access and participation in accordance with individual support plans.    Qualification & experience   Relevant Study in the field   Previous experience in a Family Support Worker, Community Support Worker, Case Worker or similar community services role for a minimum of 1 year.   Sound knowledge of person-centred practice, child and family support principles, and community service frameworks.  Ability to assess client needs, develop support plans and maintain accurate case documentation.  Strong communication, interpersonal and relationship-building skills with clients and stakeholders.  Experience working with vulnerable individuals, families, children and people with disability from diverse cultural backgrounds.  Knowledge of relevant legislation, including privacy, child protection, safeguarding and workplace health and safety requirements.  Proficiency in Microsoft Office and electronic client management systems.  Current National Police Check, Working with Children Check and NDIS Worker Screening Check (or ability to obtain).  Current First Aid and CPR Certificate.  Current Australian Driver's Licence and reliable vehicle (preferred).   About Company    BEHL HOLDINGS PTY LTD is a trusted provider of community and family support services, committed to improving the wellbeing, independence and quality of life of individuals and families. Through compassionate, person-centred care and tailored support programs, the company empowers clients to achieve positive outcomes while fostering strong community connections in a safe, inclusive and respectful environment. result.description:
EAST AVENUE ESPRESSO CAFE operates in Oatley in Southern Sydney and is well-known for its warm atmosphere and welcoming staff. With an extensive, varied and creative menu, the venue is renowned for its delicious food options, with a particular focus on generous gluten-free and vegan selections that cater to different dietary needs. We pride ourselves on our wide range menu items with all meals and components prepared in-house from our skilled team of chefs using locally sourced and fresh ingredients.

East Avenue Espresso Cafe is looking for a passionate and reliable SOUS CHEF to join our kitchen team. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment and will be able to support the Head Chef in leading and managing the kitchen.

As Sous Chef at East Avenue Espresso Cafe, you will be responsible for:

-  Assisting the Head Chef in overseeing all kitchen operations.
-  Managing food ordering and maintain appropriate stock levels.
-  Monitoring stock control and minimising waste.
-  Overseeing all food preparation/cooking, including quality and presentation control.
-  Receiving, inspecting and checking all deliveries to ensure quality and accuracy.
-  Supervising, supporting and motivating the kitchen team during service, including delegation of tasks and responsibilities.
-  Training and developing junior kitchen staff to ensure proper culinary techniques and processes at all times.
-  Work closely with the Front of House (FOH) team to ensure smooth communication and excellent customer service.
-  Menu development and costings and creating new menu ideas.
-  Ensuring compliance to all regulations, food safety standards & WHS requirements
-  Stepping up and taking full responsibility for kitchen operations in the absence of the Head Chef.

This is a full-time role with a salary of $80,000-$85,000 per year.

To be eligible for the Sous Chef position, we are looking for:

-  Trade qualifications
-  Previous experience as a Sous Chef or in a similar leadership role. (Minimum of 2 years of experience preferred.)
-  Experience in a similar venue and with similar cuisine/menus - experience with Greek cuisine is highly desirable.
-  Experience in menu/recipe development.
-  Familiarity with gluten-free, vegan and other dietary requirements and experience with gluten-free cooking.
-  Someone who stays calm under pressure and enjoys working in a fast-paced environment.
-  Great communication and teamwork skills.
-  Strong knowledge of kitchen operations, food safety, and stock management.
-  Comprehensive understanding of WHS requirements.
-  Ability to supervise and train junior kitchen staff.
-  A positive attitude and a willingness to lead and support the team.

If you're passionate about food, enjoy leading a team, and are ready for your next challenge, we'd love to hear from you. Apply now and join our team!

result.description:
Salary - 
$150,000 -  $170,000

Purpose – 
This role will lead the presales and solution consulting function for the organisation's enterprise SaaS platforms. Working at the intersection of sales, product and customers, the role is responsible for translating complex business requirements into tailored, value-led software solutions that win and grow strategic enterprise accounts. You will lead a team of solution consultants, and acts as the senior technical and commercial advisor throughout the enterprise sales cycle, with a particular focus on growth across the Asia-Pacific region, including Australia and New Zealand.

Key Responsibilities -
Solution Strategy & Deal Leadership
•	Define and own the presales and solution strategy for assigned enterprise and growth accounts across the product portfolio.
•	Lead customer discovery and requirement-gathering engagements, analysing current-state processes and designing target-state software solutions. 
•	Architect and present complex, multi-product solutions tailored to each customer's operational and commercial context. 
•	Engage senior and executive (CXO-level) stakeholders, articulating solution value through demonstrations, presentations and structured value narratives.
•	Develop return-on-investment and business-impact models that support commercial justification and value-led purchasing decisions. 
•	Support the sales organisation in qualifying, shaping and progressing opportunities through a substantial enterprise pipeline.

Team Leadership & Capability Development
•	Lead, coach and develop a team of senior presales / solution consultants, setting performance standards and supporting career growth.
•	Establish presales best practices, methodologies and quality standards for deliverables across the team.Cross-Functional Collaboration & Market Engagement.
•	Partner with the product organisation to channel structured customer feedback and influence roadmap priorities. 
•	Collaborate with sales, product, delivery and commercial teams to ensure proposed solutions are technically sound, deliverable and commercially viable.
•	Represent the organisation at industry events, forums and customer engagements to support pipeline generation and market visibility.

Selection Criteria – Skills, Qualifications & Experience
•	A bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline; a postgraduate management qualification is highly regarded.
•	Significant experience in enterprise SaaS presales, solution consulting or value engineering, including time in a leadership capacity.
•	Demonstrated success supporting and winning large, complex enterprise deals, ideally across multiple international markets.
•	Strong consultative selling, requirement-analysis, solution-design and commercial value-articulation skills.
•	Proven people-leadership experience, including managing and developing presales or solution-consulting teams.
•	Excellent communication, presentation and stakeholder-management skills, including engagement at executive level.
•	Familiarity with applying modern technologies, including generative AI, to sales and solution workflows.
•	Domain exposure to logistics, supply chain or comparable enterprise software environments is advantageous.

Scope -
The role leads a team of senior presales consultants. It carries accountability for solution outcomes on the organisation's most strategic enterprise opportunities and works closely with regional sales leadership to support revenue growth and market expansion across Asia-Pacific.

result.description:
We help people who have been involved in a car accident by handling all aspects of the claim from providing a replacement car to making sure their car is back on the road in no time.

The opportunity
We’re looking for a proven new-business sales professional who knows how to open doors, build influence, and win share with collision repairers, tow companies, vehicle dealerships and insurance brokers across Melbourne, Victoria.

If you already have strong relationships with repairers, dealers, or automotive referrers, and you’re willing to roll up your sleeves, get your hands dirty, and do what it takes to win and keep business, this role is built for you.

Reporting to the Operations Manager, you will own and grow the Victorian territory, with a primary focus on:
Winning new repairers, tow companies, dealers and insurance brokers
Expanding engagement with existing referrers
Driving sustained revenue growth through disciplined sales activity

This is a field-based, relationship-driven role where success comes from consistent prospecting, face-to-face engagement, and commercial follow-through.

You’ll plan and execute your own sales rhythm, identifying targets, booking visits, educating partners on our value proposition, and converting opportunities into long-term referrer relationships.

This role involves regular travel throughout Victoria to support new and existing accounts. From time to time, you will also travel outside Victoria to support national sales initiatives, key accounts, or strategic opportunities, working closely with the wider team. Importantly, this is not a “stay in the office” sales role. When needed, you will be on the ground supporting operations, including assisting customers, and helping resolve issues in real time. You see this as part of building trust, not someone else’s problem.

What you’ll be doing
Proactively hunting new business with collision repairers, tow companies, dealerships and insurance brokers
Leveraging existing industry relationships to accelerate growth
Building trusted partnerships through regular, structured visits
Positioning us as the preferred mobility partner
Managing your pipeline and activity through CRM with discipline and accuracy
Working closely with internal teams to deliver great outcomes for customers and partners
Travelling throughout Victoria, to support sales growth
Stepping in operationally where required – including customer interactions – to protect relationships and outcomes

What we’re looking for
This role will suit someone who is:
A true sales hunter with a track record of winning new business
Experienced selling into collision repairers, automotive dealerships, insurance brokers, or related automotive services
Well-connected in the Melbourne, Victoria repairer network (highly desirable)
Commercially minded, self-directed, and comfortable working autonomously
Practical, hands-on, and comfortable operating in the real world – not just from a CRM

You’ll also bring a valid driver’s licence with a solid driving record, a willingness to travel regularly as part of the role, strong organisational skills with disciplined follow-up, and a customer-first mindset with the resilience to confidently handle objections and complexity.

What’s in it for you
We believe in recognising great performance and supporting growth opportunities.

You’ll benefit from:
A competitive base salary with a competitive commission structure which is actually achievable, a company vehicle and fuel card
Career development and progression pathways within a growing business
A supportive leadership team that values initiative, results and empowers decision-making

Ready to drive your next chapter?
If you’re ready to lead, grow, and make a meaningful impact, we’d love to hear from you.
Apply today and take the wheel of your next great opportunity.

Employer questions
Your application will include the following questions:
Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
What's your expected annual base salary?
How much notice are you required to give your current employer?
Do you have customer service experience?
How many years' experience do you have as a Business to Business Business Development Manager?
